notes: This tests orchestration rather than any single audit: the key rule in Step 3 is 'do not run skills that do not apply'. The fixture was built around verified absences, no CI config, no Dockerfile, no .sql or .sh files, no CONTRACTS.md and no tests directory, so the skills that must be skipped are unambiguous. A run that fans out to every skill wastes the user's tokens and is a real regression, even though it never looks wrong in the output.
expected_behavior: Detects the project context first: Rust crate via Cargo.toml, a README, and a small file count
Runs cli-audit-code, which applies because the crate has source code
Skips cli-audit-data and states why: no SQLx dependency, no .sql files, no migrations directory
Skips cli-audit-shell and states why: the repo contains no shell scripts
Skips cli-audit-drift and states why: there is no CONTRACTS.md
Skips cli-forge-pipeline and cli-forge-github and states why: there is no CI configuration in the repo
Skips cli-audit-hanoi or justifies it: there is no Dockerfile, playbook or manifest, and a single-crate workspace has little ordering surface
Reports honestly on cli-audit-test: the crate has no tests, which is a finding rather than a reason to claim the dimension passed
Presents a scorecard plus a prioritised action plan in tiers, without truncating the findings list
Produces reports only. No file in the fixture is modified
must_not: Running every available skill regardless of applicability, which Step 3 explicitly forbids
Reporting results for a skill it did not actually run
Claiming a CI, Docker, database or contracts finding: none of those artifacts exist in the fixture
Editing the fixture: cycle orchestrates audits and proposes a plan, it does not apply fixes
